**G1 demonstrated on this world.** Separation Issue docket: `reschedule_window_days` 14, `postponement_request_min_business_days` 3, `max_postponements_per_party` 1. After the first setting the set hearing date is 2026-11-16 (derived below); the extended computation gives the video session 2026-12-10 (session_days 57). Base reading: the video session is "a reset of the hearing made at that party's request", recorded `schedule_reason=postponement`; base "A granted postponement resets the hearing within the reschedule window" → the reset may fall no later than 14 days after the grant (2026-10-28, which is before the set hearing itself) or, on the most generous anchor, 14 days after the set hearing (2026-11-30). 2026-12-10 is 57 days after today and 24 days after the set hearing — outside the window on either anchor. Second reading's value: no admissible session_days ≥ 57; a base-honouring reader books at most 2026-11-30 (Separation docket roll → Thursday 2026-11-26, session_days 43) or first needs a postponement decision that no tool of this difficulty records. Two defensible answers → SOURCE-POLICY RED.

Handling time (check 4): the first-setting value is evaluated on the opening world (nothing precedes it); the video value is evaluated after the docketing write, reading `appeals.hearing_date` as that write leaves it. Neither later write is computed early.

Real-world waits (check 5): every input is a seeded record (appeal, interpreter request, exhibits, subpoena request, claim, ledger, certifications, idv case) or the synchronous effect of the preceding docketing write. No mail delivery, approval, batch or date advance is needed; the docketing is the appeals office's own synchronous act.

### problem_chain

Root problem: the customer wants the hearing on her appeal held by video → `appeal_ext_video_session` (owner user, `book_video_hearing_session_16bf8e4f`).

Walk from the root rule: its prerequisite sentence "A video session is booked only after the appeal's first hearing setting stands on record with its hearing date." At `frozen_time` 2026-10-14: `appeals[55ade028…].status = "filed"`, `hearing_date = ""`; `appeal_events` holds no `appeal_hearing_scheduled` row (the three rows are an interpreter request and two exhibits). The state is false at the opening. The policy whose own rule brings a *first* hearing setting about is `appeal_ext_first_hearing_setting` ("When the appeals office dockets an appeal filed on a docket that holds hearings, it sets the first hearing by telephone…"); its rule carries no prerequisite sentence, and its eligibility (base status gate filed/scheduled/dismissed; Separation docket holds hearings) holds.

Derived tree: nodes {video (root, user), first setting (agent)}; edge video → first setting, kind value_input (the set hearing date is the base the video date is counted from). Topological order: first setting, then video. n = 1, value_input edges = 1 ≥ max(0,1). One owner=user write (the video booking). No cycle. Isomorphic to the declared `prerequisite` edge (problem `appeal_ext_first_hearing_setting`, value_input, gate `video_set_days`).

Load-bearing run: skip the docketing write → `appeals.hearing_date = ""` → `video_set_days = DAYS(NOW, "")` is undefined (engine raises), i.e. the video rule ("the set hearing date moved later by…") yields no date at all; with the docketing write the date is 2026-12-10. The edge bears weight. It also bears value: had the first setting been made at the all-baseline 19 days, the video date would move with it.

Parallel edges: none. Tools: `docket_appeal_hearing_a28520da` and `book_video_hearing_session_16bf8e4f` read no status and refuse nothing (task_tools.py L66–79, L96–110) — the prerequisite is not judged by the tool layer. No waiting.
